findings.claim: §8 R-022-13 line 680 specifies `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection/required_signatures` as the required-signed-commits toggle verb, but the GitHub REST API does not support PATCH on this endpoint. The correct verb to enable required commit signatures is POST. A Codex executor following the dispatch package instruction verbatim will issue `gh api -X PATCH …`, receive HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed, misfire the partial-apply rollback path, and report status=blocked — blocking slice 020J on every dispatch.
findings.evidence: Plan §8 R-022-13, line 680: 'required-signed-commits toggle (`PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection/required_signatures`)'. GitHub REST API for commit signature protection defines three verbs: GET (retrieve), POST (enable — 'Create commit signature protection'), DELETE (disable). There is no PATCH verb documented or accepted for this endpoint; GitHub returns 405 on an unrecognised method. The tag-protection call on line 678 correctly uses POST (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags/protection) and the rollback correctly uses DELETE (line 683). Only the required-signed-commits enable step uses the wrong verb. The verify_commands on lines 687–688 correctly use GET; the bug is in the creation/enable step only.
findings.impact: Slice 020J makes tag-protection first (POST — succeeds), then required-signed-commits toggle (PATCH — 405). The plan's own partial-apply mitigation then triggers: Codex invokes DELETE to revert the tag-protection rule and reports status=blocked with gate_failure=partial_apply_reverted. The orchestrator pauses the chain and emits a notification requiring user confirmation before re-dispatch. Since the wrong verb is baked into the plan's instruction text, re-dispatch without amending the plan repeats the same failure. Slice 020K (CODEOWNERS wiring) and 020D1 (SCP self-dogfood) both depend on 020J completing cleanly; all subsequent Track 1 slices are blocked until the verb is corrected. The required-signed-commits prerequisite for 020D1 (signed merge commit) is never satisfied.
findings.mitigation: Change line 680 from 'PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection/required_signatures' to 'POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection/required_signatures'. The GitHub REST API endpoint 'Create commit signature protection' (POST) enables the protection and returns 200 with the resource. No other change is required — the verify_commands GET form and the DELETE rollback form are both correct.

findings.claim: Plan §4.5 states that the --check-hash-chain mode of scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh 'walks both layouts' (implementation-slice flat layout and plan-slice r{N}-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json layout). The script explicitly contradicts this: its own comment at lines 360–362 states the plan-slice layout 'is NOT consumed by --check-hash-chain (which only operates on implementation slices)'. The plan's claim is false; the check only handles the implementation-slice layout.
findings.evidence: Plan §4.5 lines 426–429: 'The WP-SCP-022 plan-slice itself is the only review pack using the r{N}-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json layout per §11. The --check-hash-chain mode of scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh walks both layouts.' Script lines 357–362: '# Per plan §4.5: implementation slices use the flat layout … The plan-slice review pack itself uses r{N}-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json but that pack is NOT consumed by --check-hash-chain (which only operates on implementation slices). Closes R3 C-MAJ-01 / BYPASS-001.' The script's check_hash_chain function resolves terminal_dir to DISPATCHES_DIR/<slice-id> (line 337) or a fix-round-N subdir thereof — it has no code path for the docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/r{N}-{lens}/ directory tree used by the plan-slice. Invoking --check-hash-chain 022a would fail immediately at 'fixpoint.md missing' (exit 1) since there is no dispatches/022a/fixpoint.md.
findings.impact: An orchestrator reading §4.5 and believing the check supports both layouts might attempt --check-hash-chain 022a to verify the plan-slice's hash chain and misinterpret the exit-1 failure as a genuine chain problem rather than a missing-feature error. More broadly, the plan-slice's hash chain (in docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/r{N}-{lens}/ files) has no machine-verified integrity check; the claim that the gate script provides one is incorrect. This does not block the autonomous run (implementation slices are verified correctly) but leaves the plan-slice's own chain unverified by tooling, contrary to the plan's assertion.
findings.mitigation: Change §4.5 to accurately describe what the script does: replace 'walks both layouts' with 'operates on implementation slices only (flat layout); the plan-slice review pack at docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/r{N}-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json is not verified by this mode and must be inspected manually.' Optionally add a separate --check-plan-hash-chain mode to the script that reads the r{N}-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json layout — but this is not required to close the finding; correcting the plan text is sufficient.

findings.claim: check_hash_chain() calls require_cmd python3 sha256sum (line 303) even though python3 is not used anywhere within that function. On a Linux CI environment that has sha256sum but not python3, require_cmd returns 6 on the python3 check before reaching sha256sum; the || fallback block then looks for shasum (which Linux typically lacks), finds it absent, and returns 6 — even though sha256sum is fully available. The prerequisite check incorrectly blocks the function on a valid execution environment.
findings.evidence: Script line 303: 'require_cmd python3 sha256sum'. The require_cmd helper (lines 69–76) iterates commands and returns 6 on the first missing one. On Linux without python3 but with sha256sum, python3 is checked first → returns 6 → the || block (lines 304–309) checks for shasum (the macOS fallback) → shasum absent → return 6 → check_hash_chain exits 6 'missing prerequisite'. The hash_file helper (lines 349–355) branches correctly between sha256sum and shasum without needing python3. python3 is genuinely needed by check_no_symlink_escape (which calls resolve_real_path) but is not called by check_hash_chain.
findings.mitigation: Remove python3 from the require_cmd call in check_hash_chain: change 'require_cmd python3 sha256sum' to 'require_cmd sha256sum'. The || block already handles the macOS sha256sum-absent / shasum-present case. python3 remains correctly required by check_no_symlink_escape (called from the --slice mode) where resolve_real_path uses it.

r1_findings_closure.evidence: scripts/wp_scp_022_gate_check.sh lines 364–374: when highest < 0 (no fix rounds), the function now reads terminal_dir/review-correctness.json, terminal_dir/review-safety.json, terminal_dir/review-completeness.json — the flat §4.5 implementation-slice layout. The old r1-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json paths are absent. The fix-round branch (highest >= 0) uses the same filenames inside the fix-round-N subdir, also consistent with §4.5. Comment at lines 357–362 explicitly references 'Closes R3 C-MAJ-01 / BYPASS-001'. Both branches of the if/else are now identical in path structure, which is correct because §4.5 specifies the same filename convention for both the initial and fix-round layouts relative to their respective terminal directory.

Plan §8 R-022-13 lines 686–692 now explicitly names both required verify_commands for slice 020J: (1) gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags/protection | jq '.[] | select(.pattern=="v*")' — confirming tag-protection rule present; (2) gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection/required_signatures | jq '.enabled' returning true — confirming required-signed-commits active. Both commands are specified as mandatory, with 'Either verify failing → exit non-zero → dispatcher status overridden to blocked.' The orchestrator now has an independent check beyond Codex self-report.

Plan line 846 (document footer) now reads: '**End of plan v0.4.** Awaiting Gate C round-4 review.' The version number and round descriptor match the header at line 4 which reads 'Version: 0.4 (R3 fix-round — closes 3 R3 MAJ + 4 MIN; completeness lens already APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS at R3; awaiting R4 review)'. The v0.2/round-2 stale text is gone.

structured_review.summary: All three R3 correctness findings are verifiably closed in v0.4: R3-C-MAJ-01 (no-fix-round hash-chain path used wrong r1-{lens}/dispatcher-result.json filenames) is closed — both branches of check_hash_chain now correctly read review-{lens}.json at the appropriate terminal directory; R3-C-MIN-01 (020J verify_commands unspecified) is closed — §8 R-022-13 now names both mandatory gh api GET commands with expected return values; R3-C-nit-01 (footer version mismatch) is closed — footer now reads 'End of plan v0.4.' One new MAJ was introduced: §8 R-022-13 line 680 specifies PATCH as the HTTP verb to enable required commit signatures, but the GitHub REST API defines POST (create) as the only verb to enable this protection — PATCH returns 405, the partial-apply rollback fires, and slice 020J is blocked on every dispatch until the verb is corrected. One new MIN was introduced: §4.5 claims --check-hash-chain walks both the implementation-slice and plan-slice layouts, but the script explicitly states it only handles implementation slices; the plan-slice layout is unsupported and the claim is false. One nit: python3 is spuriously listed as a prerequisite in check_hash_chain's require_cmd call, causing incorrect exit-6 on Linux environments with sha256sum but not python3. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED.
